title: Behind MAGA’s Anti-Colonial Turn
author: Geoff Shullenberger
content:
![Behind MAGA’s Anti-Colonial
Turn](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/09/AP26255382816344.jpg)

Not long after he arrived in Ireland over the weekend, President Donald Trump
[_declared_](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/12/world/europe/trump-ireland-
unification-remarks.html?ref=compactmag.com) that it would be "fantastic" and
a "cool thing" if the island were to be politically unified, offering an
unexpected boost to the Irish republican cause. This came just a few weeks
after the administration announced it was "reviewing" its position on the
British sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, long claimed by Argentina. This
statement galvanized the Trump-allied Argentine president, Javier Milei, to
ratchet up pressure on Britain over the contested territory.

These aren't the only instances in which the Trump administration looked ready
to dismantle the remnants of old world empires. During the crisis occasioned
by the influx of migrants into the Spanish enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla,
there was speculation that Trump, who is friendlier with Rabat than Madrid
these days, might back the former's claims over those territories. Then there
is Trump's desire to end Danish rule over Greenland, which stands with the
Falklands among the few territories in the Western hemisphere still owing
fealty to a European monarch.

What is peculiar here is that, in other contexts, leading members of the
administration have expressed wistfulness about the waning of European
overseas empires. In his speech to the Munich Security Conference in February,
Secretary of State Marco Rubio fondly recalled the lost era when the West was
sending "its missionaries, its pilgrims, its soldiers, its explorers pouring
out from its shores to cross oceans, settle new continents, build vast empires
extending out across the globe." He went on to lament the "terminal decline"
of Western imperialism after World War II, which he said was "accelerated by
godless communist revolutions and by anti-colonial uprisings that would
transform the world and drape the red hammer and sickle across vast swaths of
the map."
